title: Test C and D require openssl binary at runtime; fail silently in offline CI
description: smime_tests.rs tests C (test_sign_output_accepted_by_openssl) and D (test_encrypt_output_decrypted_by_openssl) invoke std::process::Command::new('openssl') and call .expect('openssl must be available'). If openssl is not installed, the test panics with an unhelpful expect message rather than being skipped. In a minimal CI environment (e.g. a Docker container without openssl, or on Windows) both tests panic, making it look like the crate is broken when in fact the oracle tool is just absent. These tests should either skip when openssl is absent (std::process::Command::new('openssl').output().is_err()) or document the openssl requirement in the test harness setup.
close_reason: by design; openssl as test oracle is per CLAUDE.md test integrity rules
